Name: Insufficiently Controlled Parser Differential
Description:
The product uses a common specification or format that is shared
		between multiple components or entities, but the components have
		different parsers that can interpret the same input in different,
		security-relevant ways.

ModesOfIntroduction.Note:
The product's components might be required to follow a specification that is incomplete in ways that do not sufficiently cover security expectations, and/or allows for implementation-specific variations that may be security-critical. 


(All Phases: Requirements, Architecture and Design)

CommonConsequences.Note: If an input is analyzed and/or processed by multiple components in security-related situations - such as analyzing headers or comparing identifiers - then a parser differential could lead to incorrect security decisions.

DetectionMethods.Description: The different product components or entities could be tested using inputs with a variety of manipulations, such as differences in capitalization, whitespace, "boundary" tags, etc. The behavior of each component could be evaluated to see if the inputs are handled consistently.

PotentialMitigations.Description: If possible, ensure that the same parser is used by each component.
PotentialMitigations.EffectivenessNotes: This might be difficult to do if the affected product has some components or entities that are not directly under its control, such as with firewalls managing traffic between diverse systems that might have a variety of libraries across different operating systems, programming languages, etc.

ObservedExamples.Description: JavaScript-based DOM parser silently accepts certain malformed end tags such as "</a\nResidue>" due to a parser differential, possibly preventing the detection of malformed input.

A Survey of Parser Differential Anti-Patterns
